text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Wednesday morning newspapers:
- Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek met U.S. Secretary of Defence William Cohen, who said Slovenia was a serious candidate to join NATO in the first round of its expansion.
- Slovenian Railway workers held a four hour strike demanding higher wages. If further talks fail to reach an agreement, a similar strike will be held on May 13, railway unions said.
- Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler said his French counterpart Herve De Charette supported Slovenia's bid to join NATO.
- Slovenian parliamentary speaker Janez Podobnik met Austrian president Thomas Klestil.
- Representatives of the Ministry of Defence neither confirmed nor denied reports of a strike by Slovenian army officers who are demanding payment for extra hours.
- Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler starts a two-day visit to Denmark on Wednesday.
- Slovenian Minister of Economic Relations and Development Marjan Senjur said the government's control of 20 to 25 percent of all prices in the country is unacceptable.
- Slovenian glue maker Mitol will be listed on the over-the-counter section of the Ljubljana bourse from May 15.
